'''Torch Industries''' was [[Paul Todd Feldman]]'s Star Wars fan site, "Dr Torch's Web Page", hosted on AOL at members.aol.com/drtorch. The Wayback Machine captured it from December 1998 to November 2004.<ref name="idx98">[http://members.aol.com/drtorch/index.html Torch Industries Home Page], Paul Todd Feldman. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19981203090149/http://members.aol.com:80/drtorch/index.html Internet Archive] (December 1998); [https://web.archive.org/web/20041001072834/http://members.aol.com:80/drtorch/ Internet Archive] (October 2004)</ref><ref name="hof">[http://members.aol.com/drtorch/hof.html Hall of Fame], Paul Todd Feldman. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041129112812/http://members.aol.com:80/drtorch/hof.html Internet Archive] (November 2004)</ref> It had a Star Wars store for toys and cards, Kenner toy news, and '''Master the Art of Star Wars CCG''', a deck and strategy section that Feldman maintained. That section linked [[Carl Mike Hardy]]'s ''Alderaan Express''.<ref name="master">[http://members.aol.com/drtorch/master.html Master the Art of SW CCG], Paul Todd Feldman. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010815235200/http://members.aol.com:80/drtorch/master.html Internet Archive]</ref>

[[File:Torch Industries homepage 2000.png|thumb|right|300px|The Torch Industries homepage in 2000.]]

== DecipherCon team decks ==
Feldman posted two decks that won the [[DecipherCon 1999 Team Event]]:
* '''[[DecipherCon 1999 Team Event Paul Todd Feldman DS|Feldman's Drazin Deck]]''' ([[Dark]], [[Carbon Chamber Testing / My Favorite Decoration|Carbon Chamber Testing]]), built around [[Corporal Drazin]]. He called it an interactive deck that "goes everywhere and fights".<ref name="drazin">[http://members.aol.com/drtorch/ErikDark.html Feldman's Drazin Deck: Decipher Con Team Play Winning Deck], Paul Todd Feldman. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000303173004/http://members.aol.com:80/drtorch/ErikDark.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''[[DecipherCon 1999 Team Event Paul Todd Feldman LS|Feldman's Harvest]]''' ([[Light]], [[Harvest]]), which starts with Obi-Wan's Hut and Lars' Moisture Farm. A version of it won him a Regional and the DecipherCon team event.<ref name="harvest">[http://members.aol.com/drtorch/Erik.html Feldman's Harvest Deck: Regional Qualifier/DecipherCon Team Winning Deck], Paul Todd Feldman. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011105084834/http://members.aol.com:80/drtorch/Erik.html Internet Archive]</ref>

The site also listed a team, "Dark Force Rising": Feldman, [[Jeff Davis]], [[Jeff Field]] and [[Dan Hammond]], with [[Eric Field]] as alternate.<ref name="rising">[http://members.aol.com/drtorch/rising.html Dark Force Rising], Paul Todd Feldman. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991022071037/http://members.aol.com:80/drtorch/rising.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== World Championship decks ==
The site reprinted World Championship decks. From 1997: Paul Todd Feldman ([[1997 Decipher World Championship Paul Todd Feldman DS|DS]], [[1997 Decipher World Championship Paul Todd Feldman LS|LS]]), Joe Alread ([[1997 Decipher World Championship Joe Alread DS|DS]], [[1997 Decipher World Championship Joe Alread LS|LS]]), Michael Krause ([[1997 Decipher World Championship Michael Krause DS|DS]], [[1997 Decipher World Championship Michael Krause LS|LS]]), Michael Riboulet ([[1997 Decipher World Championship Michael Riboulet DS|DS]], [[1997 Decipher World Championship Michael Riboulet LS|LS]]) and Philipp Jacobs ([[1997 Decipher World Championship Philipp Jacobs DS|DS]], [[1997 Decipher World Championship Philipp Jacobs LS|LS]]). From 1999: James Lafferty ([[1999 Decipher World Championship James Lafferty DS|DS]], [[1999 Decipher World Championship James Lafferty LS|LS]]), Steven Lewis ([[1999 Decipher World Championship Steven Lewis DS|DS]], [[1999 Decipher World Championship Steven Lewis LS|LS]]), Gary Carman ([[1999 Decipher World Championship Gary Carman DS|DS]], [[1999 Decipher World Championship Gary Carman LS|LS]]) and Clint Hays ([[1999 Decipher World Championship Clint Hays LS|LS]]).<ref name="master" />

== Top 10 and Hall of Fame ==
'''Top 10 Players''' was Feldman's personal ranking. He left himself off and wrote that "it is only my opinion". In order: [[Ray Bordier]], [[Brian Hunter]], [[James Lafferty|James Laferty]], [[Steve Brentson]], [[Clint Hays]], [[Martin Falke]], [[Steven Lewis|Steve Lewis]], [[Yannick Lapointe]], [[Gary Carman|Gary Carmen]] and Jeff Field.<ref name="top">[http://members.aol.com/drtorch/Top.html Dr Torch's Top 10], Paul Todd Feldman. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991013000328/http://members.aol.com:80/drtorch/Top.html Internet Archive]</ref>

His '''Hall of Fame''', which he "created for fun one day", ranked from 10th to 1st: [[Philipp Jacobs|Phillip Jacobs]], [[Stuart Jones]], [[Gary Carman]], [[Maarten Logghe]], [[Raphael Asselin|Rafael Asselian]], [[Jon VanDerMeer|Jon Vandermeer]], [[Brian Hunter]], [[Kevin Reitzel|Kevin Reitzal]], [[Joe Alread]] and Feldman himself.<ref name="hof" />

== Jabba's Palace pre-release ==
[[File:Torch Industries Jabba's Palace pre-release banner.jpg|thumb|right|The pre-release banner.]]
The site announced the [[1998 Jabba's Palace Pre-Release (Mountain View)|Jabba's Palace pre-release tournament]] for 25 April 1998 at Match Play in Mountain View, California. [[Carl Mike Hardy]] (Red 32) was the tournament director.<ref name="pre">[http://members.aol.com/drtorch/pre.html Jabba's Pre-release], Paul Todd Feldman. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991022042653/http://members.aol.com:80/drtorch/pre.html Internet Archive]</ref>
